description: VN adjective-predicate copula drop (A2 build gate). Rule en-vn-copula-be-adjective inserts the missing copula in narrow bare-adjective surfaces with pronoun or single-token named subjects. It is intentionally stricter than en-be-verb-omission: this fixture locks the no-intensifier adjective gap only, not the existing 'very + adjective' rule.
fp_risk_note: High risk. Bare adjective predicates overlap with bare verbs, noun predicates, and sentence fragments. V1 stays narrow by using a closed adjective whitelist, accepting only pronoun subjects plus a single-token capitalized name surface, rejecting common non-name sentence starters, and refusing already-correct be forms. The negative cases lock the bare-verb and noun-predicate confusables.

positive.notes: Plural subject -> inserts 'are' and preserves trailing time adverb.
Single-token named subject -> past marker triggers 'was'.

negative.notes: Bare verb confusable; the rule must not insert 'be'.
Already-correct copula form must stay unchanged.
Already-correct plural copula form must stay unchanged.
Noun-predicate / common-noun subject surface must not be rewritten by a pronoun/name-only rule.
Named subject + bare verb remains outside the adjective whitelist.
A very-surface outside the existing be-drop adjective whitelist must stay unchanged; this new rule must not overlap.
Overlap boundary: the older 'very + adjective' rule owns this surface, so the new rule must abstain while the existing be-drop rule still fires.

Over-fire boundary: a whitelisted adjective ('kind') used ATTRIBUTIVELY to modify a noun ('people') needs no copula — the adjective is not the sentence-final predicate, so the rule must abstain and not insert 'are' before it.
